attempts.paper_title: A Neural Population Mechanism for Rapid Learning
attempts.entry_title: PMd and M1 population structure in Baseline reaching (Perich, Gallego and Miller 2018)
attempts.summary: The dataset holds only the Baseline epoch, so the paper's central claims about curl field and rotation adaptation, including output-null activity failing to generalize in the curl field only, could not be tested. Two Baseline findings were partly supported. PMd was higher-dimensional than M1 in every session, but the medians were below the paper's, and this rests on an assumed noise scale. Output-null activity led output-potent, significantly only under one reading of the kernel width, with a smaller lag than the paper's. Minor checks on dimensionality across sample sizes and the null/potent index held, but pooled counts of units above 5 Hz fell short. I did not create `summaries/000688-perich-2018-01.md`.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Perich, Gallego and Miller (2018) that can be tested on dandiset 000688. The dandiset holds the Baseline epoch only of the dual-array center-out sessions of Monkeys C and M, without the curl field, visuomotor rotation and Washout trials, and without labels saying which sessions are the paper's. It tests the unit counts, the dimensionality of the PMd and M1 manifolds, the null/potent index of PMd neurons, and the lag between output-null and output-potent activity in Baseline.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Perich et al. (2018) from dandiset 000688

outcomes.notes: Measured values are over all 21 candidate sessions. Monkey M's 7 sessions give 66 to 121 PMd and 26 to 52 M1 units, inside the widened ranges. 13 of 14 Monkey C candidates are inside (PMd 137 to 258, M1 55 to 95); C 2016-09-29 has 114 PMd units, below the lower bound of 123.3. The ranges hold for 715 of the 2002 choices of 9 Monkey C sessions, those without C 2016-09-29, which is the assumption the outcome rests on. The pooled counts above 5 Hz hold under no choice of 9 Monkey C sessions with the 7 Monkey M sessions (at most 634 M1 and 1224 PMd against 918 and 2221); all 21 sessions give 835 M1 (within 10%) and 1565 PMd (outside). Rates over all trials of a file change the counts by at most 10. Monkey M has 6 to 21 PMd units above 5 Hz per session. The pooled verdicts of the first table in the notebook are for each whole set (21 or 19 sessions); the test on 16 sessions is the second cell.
deviations: The paper's 16 sessions cannot be identified. All 21 dual-array center-out sessions of Monkeys C (2016-09-09 to 2016-10-21) and M (2014-02-03 to 2014-03-07) are used, and the 19 whose reward counts fit the paper's Baseline range (154 to 225) are shown as a second set. All reward trials of each file are taken as Baseline.

The 5 Hz rule uses the trials in the file (Baseline only), from start to stop of each reward trial; all trials are shown as a variant. The paper's rate is over the whole session (claims file criterion).
The paper excluded cells with high coincidence across channels; the units are counted as deposited.

outcomes.notes: Over all 21 sessions, under rule (b), window (a), the noise of the trial average and a kernel of 100 ms standard deviation, the medians are 7 (M1) and 10 (PMd), outside the tolerance of 8.5 and 14, and PMd exceeds M1 in 21 of 21 sessions (19 of 19 in the second set, medians 7 and 11). Over the 2002 choices of 16 sessions (9 of the 14 Monkey C candidates with the 7 Monkey M sessions) the medians are 7 to 7.5 and 10 to 11, outside tolerance in every choice, with PMd above M1 in every session in all 2002; the closest session is M 2014-03-03 (PMd 9, M1 8). By monkey C has medians 7 and 10, M 7 and 11. Under this kernel no reading meets the criterion in full; window (b) gives PMd above M1 in 20 of 21, rule (a) in 19 and 18 of 21 with medians of 26 to 47 (M1) and 46 to 78 (PMd). With a kernel of 100 ms full width at half maximum the medians are 9 and 13 over 21 sessions, within tolerance in 910 of the 2002 choices, which would be reproduced. On synthetic rank-5 data rule (b) with the adopted noise scale returns 5 in 9 of 9 runs and rule (a) 16 to 45. Raw or root-two noise gives 0 dimensions in every session. The outcome was reproduced (full-width reading) through round 2 and changed in round 3, when the verifier agreed with the proposed change.
deviations: The paper's 16 sessions cannot be identified. All 21 dual-array center-out sessions of Monkeys C (2016-09-09 to 2016-10-21) and M (2014-02-03 to 2014-03-07) are used, and the 19 whose reward counts fit the paper's Baseline range (154 to 225) are shown as a second set, with every choice of 16 sessions. All reward trials of each file are taken as Baseline.

Target acquisition (window a, the claims file's O3) is the trial's stop time minus the 0.5 s target hold, from STAR Methods, Behavioral task ("required to hold there for 0.5 s"); the cursor cannot be used, as in several sessions it never enters the stored target square.

Assumed that the noise eigenvalues are scaled to the noise of a trial average (the difference of two trials divided by the square root of 2K, K the mean number of trials per target). STAR Methods, Dimensionality reduction, says only that the activity of random pairs of trials was subtracted; taken as it is, or divided by the square root of two, the noise exceeds every component of the trial-averaged data and every estimate is 0, which cannot give the paper's medians. All three scalings are shown. The choice was made after the raw and root-two scales gave 0; a synthetic check of known rank (notebook) shows rule (b) with this scale recovers the rank, but the raw and root-two scales also recover it there, so the check does not choose between the scales; the choice rests on the other scales giving 0 on the real data.

The outcome depends on the kernel width, which the claims file expected not to matter (O4). Assumed a standard deviation of 100 ms for every claim, as the usual way a Gaussian smoothing kernel's width is stated and the way the same group states it in a later paper on Monkey C recordings ("a Gaussian kernel (s.d. 50 ms)", Gallego, Perich et al. 2020, Nat. Neurosci.). STAR Methods, Dimensionality reduction, says only "a non-causal Gaussian kernel of width 100 ms". With a full width at half maximum of 100 ms the medians are within tolerance and the claim would be reproduced, while fig6c-null-leads-potent would be not reproduced; neither reading favours every claim. The claims file's header says a claim whose open-detail readings disagree is blocked as methods_underspecified; the protocol (author, step 1.6) instead lets the author adopt the best-supported reading as an assumption, and that rule is followed.
Trials of unequal length are aligned on the window start and cut to the session's shortest window before averaging per target; the paper does not say how they were averaged (a standard choice).
All units of each area are used; the paper does not say whether a rate threshold applies here.

outcomes.notes: Under rule (b) the mean PMd dimensionality exceeds the mean M1 at 40, 50, 60, 70 and all neurons under both kernels, both windows and both session sets, by 1.30 to 4.63 (full-width kernel, window a, 1.88 at 40 and 4.52 with all neurons; standard-deviation kernel, window a, 1.62 and 3.48). Paired by session, PMd is higher in every session at every size except one session with all neurons in window (b) under both kernels (20 of 21) and one at 40 neurons with the full-width kernel in window (b) (16 of 17). Rule (a) gives PMd above M1 at every size except 40 neurons with the full-width kernel in window (b) (-0.13 and -0.30). The PMd mean falls at small sizes (window a, full-width kernel, 13.05 with all neurons and 9.90 at 40). The M1 mean does not fall consistently (window a, full-width kernel, 8.52 with all, 8.53 and 8.65 at 60 and 70, 8.03 at 40; window b, full-width kernel, 6.52 with all and 6.74 at 40), so the statement's fall is shown for PMd only, outside the criterion. The M1 means at 40 neurons cover 17 sessions, against 21 for all neurons. M1 sizes of 50 to 70 rest on 11 to 15 sessions, as Monkey M has 26 to 52 M1 units.

outcomes.notes: Over 3263 PMd units of 21 sessions, with absolute values, the mean index is 0.017 to 0.056 across the window and kernel readings and no unit exceeds 0.9 in absolute value (range -0.701 to 0.741). With sums of squares three of four readings meet the criterion; window (a) with the full-width kernel gives a mean of 0.100085, just above 0.1, with 0.09% of units above 0.9. The shuffled control has mean 0.036, standard deviation 0.483 (data 0.217) and 3.2% of units above 0.9. The index leans positive in Monkey M, whose 599 units have a mean of 0.109 under the main reading (above 0.1 if judged alone; session means 0.081 to 0.143), against 0.028 for the 2664 Monkey C units (session means -0.007 to 0.081).

Target acquisition (window a, the claims file's O3) is the trial's stop time minus the 0.5 s target hold, from STAR Methods, Behavioral task ("required to hold there for 0.5 s"); the cursor cannot be used, as in several sessions it never enters the stored target square.

The readings of magnitude disagree in one of eight cases; the sum of absolute values, the claims file's first reading of "the magnitude ... summed across all dimensions" (STAR Methods, Output-potent and output-null subspaces), is adopted.

The one failing reading (sums of squares, window a) uses the full-width kernel. Under the standard-deviation kernel, the reading adopted for every claim, all four window and magnitude readings meet the criterion.

outcomes.notes: Over the 21 candidate sessions the mean Baseline lag is negative under all 8 readings (-2.4 to -51.4 ms). It is significantly negative only with window (a) and the 100 ms standard-deviation kernel, at -18.1 ms (t = -2.29, p = 0.033, 10 ms resolution) and -51.4 ms (p = 0.035, interpolated 50 ms activity); in the latter two sessions peak within one step of the edge of the search (C 2016-10-06 at -350 ms, C 2016-10-11 at -340 ms), and without them the mean is -20.5 ms over 19 sessions (p = 0.034). The full-width kernel and window (b) readings give p from 0.18 to 0.82. No reading over 21 sessions is within 3.5 ms of -35 ms. Over the 2002 choices of 16 sessions (9 of the 14 Monkey C candidates with the 7 Monkey M sessions) the main reading is significantly negative in 763 (38%), the 50 ms reading in 478 (816 with edge maxima dropped), and at least one of the 8 readings in 1013 (51%; 1052 with edge maxima dropped); 12 choices, all with edge maxima dropped at 50 ms resolution, give a significant mean within tolerance of -35 ms. The 19-session set gives p = 0.040 for the main reading. By monkey, -22.9 ms (C) and -8.6 ms (M). The end-of-Force part of the statement cannot be tested, as no Force trials are in the dandiset; the outcome follows the criterion's partial rule on the 21 candidates (significantly negative under one reading, outside tolerance) and holds for about half of the possible 16-session sets.

All reward trials of each file are taken as Baseline.
The t-test is run over all 21 candidate sessions, a superset of the paper's 16, which the outcome rests on; the same test on every choice of 16 sessions is shown.

Significance holds with a standard deviation of 100 ms and not with a full width at half maximum of 100 ms (p 0.18 to 0.38), which would make it not reproduced. The claims file's header says a claim whose open-detail readings disagree is blocked as methods_underspecified; the protocol (author, step 1.6) lets the author adopt the best-supported reading as an assumption, and that rule is followed. The standard deviation is adopted for every claim, as the usual way a Gaussian kernel's width is stated and the form the same group used later on Monkey C recordings ("s.d. 50 ms", Gallego, Perich et al. 2020). Under it fig3b-pmd-higher-dimensional is partially reproduced.
The lag sign follows the Figure 6B legend (a peak left of zero means output-null leads).
A maximum within one step of the edge of the lag search (340 or 350 ms) is flagged and the test is shown with such sessions kept and dropped; the paper does not say how edge maxima were treated.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds about 200 reward trials per dual-array center-out session of Monkeys C and M, the size of the paper's Baseline epoch, with steady reach errors. The Force, Rotation and Washout epochs that 23 of the paper's 28 findings rest on are not in it.

No file or metadata field says which sessions were curl field or visuomotor rotation sessions, which epoch the trials belong to, or which 16 sessions the paper analysed. Monkey C has 14 candidate sessions for the paper's 9.

In seven Monkey C sessions (2016-09-09 to 2016-09-23) the cursor ends rewarded reaches about 4.2 cm from the center, with peak speeds near 14 cm/s, while target_corners places every target at 8 cm and the later sessions end at about 7.9 cm with peak speeds near 25 cm/s. The paper says Monkey C's first three sessions used 6 cm targets, which fits neither.

The session description of the seven Monkey C sessions from 2016-09-09 to 2016-09-23 ends in a cut-off warning ("Warning: This session with Monkey"), in the files and in the archive's metadata, so what it warns of is lost. These are the sessions whose cursor positions do not match the stored targets.
In all seven early Monkey C sessions the cursor never enters the square given by target_corners on rewarded trials, and in Monkey M 2014-02-03 and 2014-02-18 it enters it on 1% of them.
The cursor timestamps repeat 8531 times in C 2016-09-23 and 5014 times in C 2016-10-11, so velocities computed from them are undefined on many samples.

Units above 5 Hz are far fewer than the paper reports, at most 634 M1 and 1224 PMd for any choice of 16 candidate sessions, against 918 and 2221. Monkey M has 6 to 21 PMd units above 5 Hz per session.

Question for the authors. How was the noise scaled in the dimensionality estimate adapted from Machens et al. (2010)? The Methods subtract random pairs of trials; taken as it is, that noise exceeds every component of the trial-averaged rates and gives 0 dimensions. This attempt assumed the noise of the trial average (difference over the square root of 2K) and the 95% rule, which gives medians of 7 and 10 with a kernel of 100 ms standard deviation (9 and 13 with a full width at half maximum of 100 ms).

Question for the authors. Is the 100 ms width of the Gaussian kernel its standard deviation or its full width at half maximum, and how were trials of unequal length averaged? With the full width the dimensionality medians are 9 and 13 (paper 8.5 and 14) and the Baseline lag is not significant; with the standard deviation the medians are 7 and 10 and the lag is significantly negative over 21 sessions. This attempt assumed the standard deviation for every claim.
The dandiset holds 14 dual-array Monkey C sessions where the paper used 9, and does not say how they relate to the paper's sessions or why the perturbation epochs were left out.
